**Title:** Which Dollar Broke? Separating Token Failures from Platform-Ledger Failures in Web Dollar Markets

**Abstract (211 words):**

Web price feeds and on-chain oracles combine exchange quotes as if every USD price were in the same dollar, but an exchange's dollar is a balance in its own ledger that reaches the banking system only through the platform's rails. When those rails fail, a feed can report a platform failure as a market move, and existing work on feed reliability and cross-exchange price gaps does not separate a failing token from a failing platform ledger. The separation is hard because a ledger's value is never quoted directly, public prices thin out under stress, and any single asset may carry its own shock. We propose a decomposition that prices the platform's dollar through unpegged assets against venues whose rails stay open, and accepts the split only when unrelated assets and the venue's internal cross-rates agree. Across banking-rail episodes on three platforms between 2017 and 2023, with stablecoin runs as contrasts, the method attributes the largest dislocations to the platform's ledger rather than to tokens. A feed filter built on it removes 88% of the hours in which a naive multi-exchange index was off by 100 bps or more, and in one episode the signal appeared months before the loss behind it was disclosed. The findings are descriptive and use public data.

**Suggested keywords:** stablecoins; platform money; exchange ledgers; price feeds and oracles; Web measurement; natural experiment; reproducibility
